theory.intro: A transversal makes angle pairs whose names come from where they sit. The lines do not need to be parallel for the pairs to have these names.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Angles $11$ and $15$ occupy matching corners on the same side of the transversal: **corresponding**.

(b) Angles $13$ and $16$ are inside the two lines, on opposite sides of the transversal: **alternate**.

(c) Angles $14$ and $16$ are inside the two lines, on the same side of the transversal: **co-interior**.

These names describe positions even when the crossed lines are not parallel.

The crossed lines are not parallel.
Identify the relationship between angles $4$ and $8$.
